title: Photo 097 · 아워글래스 SSBBW · 탈라베라 · 옆으로 누운 자세 · 흑인 20대 후반
prompt:
Image format: a horizontal landscape-orientation photograph, 3:2 aspect ratio, wider than it is tall.

A full-body photograph on a plain seamless mid-grey backdrop, nothing in the frame but a low flat platform, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side so the texture of the skin stands out, sharp focus from head to toe, realistic photographic grain — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subject: ONE real adult Black woman in her late 20s, deep near-black skin tone, THE ABSOLUTE DARKEST BLACK SKIN ON EARTH, void complexion, not brown, not lightened, her face exactly as dark as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, a high swinging ponytail tied with a cord, a calm confident expression, real living eyes. She wears thick gold cuff earrings and has long oval nails with a mirror finish.

Physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person, her body so long and vast that her head and her feet are cut off by the left and right edges of the frame. A colossal heavy bust far wider than her shoulders, and below it a waistline that still draws in clearly even at this size — a shadowed groove running around her middle, the one place on her body where the outline pulls inward. Below that waistline a great mass of soft heavy fat sits on her middle and, even as she lies on her side, spills forward away from her body and hangs over the front edge of her torso under its own weight, the lowest part sagging down onto the platform, gathering into two or three heavy rounded folds stacked one in front of the other, deep shadowed creases between them, the surface soft and uneven, never taut, never smooth, never round like a drum. It merges seamlessly into her sides, her hips and her thighs with no boundary anywhere, one continuous body rather than a separate mass, not pregnant. Enormous round hips more than three times the width of that waistline and far wider than her shoulders, a gigantic rounded rear, gigantic soft thighs pressing together down to the knees, huge soft calves, very thick soft arms, a full round face. Her head looks small on top of her massive body and her hands look small against her thighs. Wide at the bust, drawn in at the waistline, wide again below: the silhouette reads as a great hourglass at the most extreme size. Every fold and curve keeps its own clear rounded outline with a deep shadowed crease between them, never merging into one shapeless mass. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other. The flesh is young and firm for its size, each fold holding a taut rounded shape. The sheer weight of the flesh is visible in how it spills forward, sags downward and presses flat against the platform beneath her.

Skin: Real photographic skin — visible pores and fine grain, a smooth taut surface with natural creases and shadow only where the flesh folds, faint stretch marks where the great curves have expanded, the raking light picking out every ridge and hollow of the surface. No smooth illustration finish, no plastic CG sheen.

Body Art: Her bare skin is painted in Mexican Talavera ceramic style — a glossy white tin glaze ground painted with bold cobalt blue, marigold yellow, terracotta orange and green floral rosettes, star medallions and scalloped borders, a thick cobalt border following every deep crease and curving around the hips and thighs. The paint is pigment sitting on living skin, so it distorts slightly over every bulge and cracks a little where the skin folds. The paint covers her whole body with no bare skin left anywhere below the jaw: her shoulders, her upper arms, her forearms and the backs of her hands are painted as densely as her torso, and so are the sides of her body, her back, her rear, the lower belly, the knees, the calves and the tops of her feet. Her face is left unpainted and the pattern fades out at the neck with no hard line.

Pose: Lying on her side on the platform facing the camera, her head resting on her raised hand with that elbow planted on the platform behind her body so her arm never crosses in front of her torso, her other arm lifted clear of her body and resting lightly on the top of her hip with the elbow raised, a visible gap of background between that arm and her side so the whole curve of her waist, hip and belly reads unbroken, her legs stacked one on the other with the knees slightly bent, her upper hip rising as a great rounded mound higher than her own shoulder and the underside hip and thigh flattening wide where they press against the platform, her body stretching across the full width of the frame from edge to edge.

Footwear: Extreme cobalt-blue square-toe platform stiletto mules, the platform soles as tall as her ankle bones, the ultra-thin stiletto heels so high her insteps stand nearly vertical.

Background & Lighting: the cobalt and marigold blazing on the white glaze, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve.

Horizontal 3:2 landscape-orientation full-body photograph, wider than it is tall.
